title: PriBeL-Net: Extending Betel Leaf Dataset with CNN-Based Image Classification
author: Mane, Bhise, et al.
materials: After training, the performance of the CNN models: MobileNetV2, EfficientNetB0, ResNet50V2, and DenseNet121 was neatly evaluated on the dataset with metrics such as Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-score. As shown in Table 5, the evaluation values are mentioned. The DenseNet121 model had the best values among the other metrics, not only on the Controlled Environment set but also, more importantly, on the On-Field set. From this comparison, one can learn that the model EfficientNetB0 shows poor performance; its accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are relatively lower in both sets. On the contrary, DenseNet121 appears to be the best model throughout, excelling with high performance at distinguishing between healthy, diseased, and dried leaves. steps.title: Download and organize dataset
steps.instruction: Obtain the PriBeL betel leaf dataset from https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/btdym2t6mt/1. The dataset is pre‑stratified into Controlled Environment (CE) and On‑Field (OF) domains. For CE there are 893 images total: 803 for training (299 healthy, 198 diseased, 306 dried) and 90 for testing (34 healthy, 22 diseased, 34 dried). For OF there are 907 images total: 815 for training (302 healthy, 260 diseased, 253 dried) and 92 for testing (34 healthy, 29 diseased, 29 dried).

steps.title: Split data and create generators
steps.instruction: From each domain split 90 % of the images for training and carve out 10 % of the training set for validation using Keras ImageDataGenerator; keep the remaining 10 % as the test set.

steps.title: Preprocess images
steps.instruction: Resize every image to 224 × 224 × 3 (RGB) and normalize pixel values by dividing by 255 (i.e., pixel/255).

steps.title: Set common training parameters
steps.instruction: Use a batch size of 32 and train for 32 epochs. Compile models with the Adam optimizer, categorical cross‑entropy loss, and accuracy as the evaluation metric.

steps.title: Build model architectures
steps.instruction: Load ImageNet‑pretrained weights for each backbone, remove the original top classification layer, add a Global Average Pooling (GAP) layer, then add model‑specific classifier layers:

substeps.instruction: MobileNetV2 – freeze the convolutional base; add GAP → Dense(3) with softmax.
EfficientNetB0 – keep the convolutional base fully trainable; add GAP → Dense(128, ReLU) → Dense(3) softmax.
ResNet50V2 – freeze the convolutional base; add GAP → Dense(128, ReLU) → Dense(3) softmax.
DenseNet121 – keep the convolutional base fully trainable; add GAP → Dense(128, ReLU) → Dense(3) softmax.

steps.title: Train models on Google Colab
steps.instruction: Run each model on Google Colab (Runtime: Python 3, Hardware accelerator: CPU) using the same hardware configuration. Record wall‑clock training time (minutes) and inference time (seconds) for the full test set with batch size 32:

substeps.instruction: MobileNetV2 – CE: 33.75 min training, 30 s inference; OF: 154.58 min training, 41 s inference.
EfficientNetB0 – CE: 19.16 min training, 23 s inference; OF: 148.03 min training, 24 s inference.
ResNet50V2 – CE: 97.18 min training, 30 s inference; OF: 111.12 min training, 30 s inference.
DenseNet121 – CE: 24.21 min training, 48 s inference; OF: 401.58 min training, 52 s inference.
